Direct Standardization

Source: R/transfer.R
ds.Rd

Transfers spectra from one instrument (the slave) to another (the master) by direct standardization (DS; Wang et al., 1991): a linear map of the whole slave spectrum onto the whole master spectrum, estimated on transfer samples measured on both instruments.

Usage

ds(x1, x2, ncomp = NULL, tol = 1e-08)

Arguments

x1

The spectra of the transfer samples on the master instrument: a numeric matrix or data frame, one spectrum per row.

x2

The spectra of the same samples, in the same order, on the slave instrument.

ncomp

The number of singular vectors of the slave spectra kept. By default, all those with a singular value above tol times the largest.

tol

The relative tolerance on the singular values. Default is 1e-8.

Value

An object of class specproc_transfer. Use predict() to transfer slave spectra.

Details

With the transfer spectra centered by the mean of each instrument, \(\textbf{X}_1 \approx \textbf{X}_2 \textbf{F}\), and the transfer matrix is \(\textbf{F} = \textbf{X}_2^{+} \textbf{X}_1\), where \(\textbf{X}_2^{+}\) is the pseudo-inverse of the slave spectra, truncated to their first ncomp singular vectors. A new slave spectrum is transferred as \(\bar{x}_1 + (x_2 - \bar{x}_2) \textbf{F}\).

With as many components as the transfer samples allow (ncomp = NULL), the transfer spectra are reproduced exactly, and the noise of the slave spectra is amplified: fewer components give a smoother, more robust transfer. Unlike pds(), DS mixes all wavelengths, so it corrects global differences of the response but needs more transfer samples. The transfer matrix (\(p \times p\)) is kept in factored form, as ncomp columns of each factor.

References

  • Wang, Y., Veltkamp, D.J., Kowalski, B.R. (1991). Multivariate instrument standardization. Analytical Chemistry, 63(23):2750-2756.

See also

pds(), sst(), slope_bias(), predict.specproc_transfer()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

data(forageLIBS)
wl <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(names(forageLIBS)))
spectra <- as.matrix(forageLIBS[which(wl > 760 & wl < 780)])  # the K I lines
# a second instrument, with a shifted and less sensitive response
slave <- 0.8 * cbind(spectra[, -1], spectra[, ncol(spectra)]) + 50
transfer <- ds(spectra[1:30, ], slave[1:30, ], ncomp = 10)
transfer
#> Direct standardization (30 transfer samples, 245 wavelengths)
#> Components: 10
# the other samples, measured on the slave, transferred to the master
transferred <- predict(transfer, slave[31:368, ])
mean(abs(transferred - spectra[31:368, ])) / mean(spectra)
#> [1] 0.02327181
